Author Ryan Holiday tells Rogan, in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, about the life of Marcus Aurelius. Holiday runs the Daily Stoic, which brings ancient Stoic thought to modern readers. The Roman emperor who wrote meditations in war camps is his central figure.

Holiday sketches the emperor's life: the throne he never wanted, the plagues and wars of his reign, and the private notebook that outlived an empire. Rogan asks what a stressed modern listener can steal from him. The segment is a warm, compact portrait of Stoicism's most tested student, told by its best-known living teacher.

Randall Carlson joins Joe Rogan for episode 1772 of the Joe Rogan Experience, one of his long marathon talks. Carlson is a self-taught researcher of geology, ancient floods, and comet impacts. His visits are known for dense maps, charts, and hours of detail.

Carlson lays out his view that giant floods and impacts wiped out early human cultures. He ties ice age disasters to myths of a great deluge found around the world. Rogan follows the evidence trail and asks where mainstream geology disagrees. Listeners who like deep, patient arguments about Earth's violent past will find plenty here.
